The suffix *ktvā* is applied after roots ending in *i*, *a*, *kṛ*, and *gam*, provided that the suffix *du* does not follow.

In the neuter, the suffixes *ṇiC*, *śas*, and those beginning with vowels (sarvanāmasthāna) undergo vowel-lengthening; however, this does not occur before the particle *bhoḥ*, before the verb *bhū*, or before a verbal suffix (*tiṅ*), except in the case of the *luṭ* (future) tense.
In the *luṭ* [future] tense,
the suffixes of *dadāti* and *ḍukr̥ñ* are *tha* and *sthaś* respectively.
From the root *smarati*, *sumara*;
from *paśyati* (here *dr̥ś*), *pēkkha*;
from *asti*, *accha*.
In the place of *ti*, *pāt*, *tha*, *bhaviṣyati*,
*mip*, and *ssaṃ*, there is optionally the lengthening of the vowel.
In the feminine, it is *itthī* for *itthi*,
and likewise *jēvva* for *jevva*.

After the verbal roots *as*, *ad*, *jas*, *vaca*, and all nominal stems (*sarvanāman*), as well as after the root *vid* (in the sense of knowing), the Parasmaipada endings are used when expressing the state (*bhāva*), the agent (*kartṛ*), or the object (*karman*).
And for this very reason,
[the substitution of *e* occurs] for the *mip* ending and for the *loṭ* imperative.
The *āścarya* (the wonderful) is by nature like the *āccharia* (the miraculous), with the remainder [of its characteristics] like the *māhārāṣṭrī* regarding the teeth on the swing-pole.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "The Characteristics of Śaurasenī," in the *Prākṛtaprakāśa* composed by Vararuci.
